message.content:
Paris has many iconic landmarks, but if you’re looking for **the single “most famous” spot**, it’s almost always the **Eiffel Tower** (La Tour eifflé).  

*Why it tops the list:*  
- It was built as a temporary structure for the 1889 Exposition Universelle and quickly became a symbol of French ingenuity.  
- Every year millions of visitors climb its three levels—or simply enjoy the view from below—making it one of the world’s most photographed monuments.  
- Its silhouette is instantly recognizable worldwide; even people who have never been to France will know what it looks like.

Other contenders include:

| Landmark | Why it matters |
|----------|----------------|
| **Louvre Museum** | Home to thousands of masterpieces including the Mona Lisa. |
| **Notre‑Dame de Paris** | Gothic cathedral famed for its architecture and tragic fire history. |
| **Sacré‑Coeur & Montmartre** | Bohemian hilltop church offering panoramic views. |

But when someone says “I’m going to Paris,” they usually mean seeing the Eiffel Tower first—and often again!
